The nine-year-old Phrygian woman, and Titias together: [concerning] the so-called Idaean Dactyls, he says that these were the first and the assessors of the mother of the gods, following Maeandrius who says that the Milesians, whenever they sacrifice to Rhea, sacrifice first to Titias and Cyllenus. These are the leaders of the Idaean Dactyls and the assessors of the mother of the gods. But Callistratus in the second book of his On Heraclea says about Titias (fg 2 M. IV 354): 'Titias is a local hero, whom some mythologize as a child of Zeus, but others as the eldest of the children of Mariandynus, son of Cimmerius, through whom especially the nation has grown and is still advancing to prosperity;'
